title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Chenin Blanc
objectives: Pair dry and sweet Chenin with food

steps.title: Dry and sweet
steps.body: Dry Chenin suits pork, chicken, river fish with butter sauce, goat's cheese and mildly spiced dishes. Off-dry Vouvray suits Thai food, pork with apples and spicy Asian dishes. Sweet Layon and Quarts de Chaume suit fruit tarts, blue cheese and foie gras. Sparkling Chenin suits aperitifs.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve dry Chenin at 10 to 12 degrees, sweet at 8 to 10. Fresh styles are best young. Top dry Vouvray and Savennières age 20 years or more; sweet Chenin from great vintages 50 years or more, thanks to acidity.
steps.highlight: Sweet Chenin ages 50 years or more

steps.prompt: Which dish suits an off-dry Vouvray?
steps.explanation: A touch of sweetness and high acidity calm the spice.

steps.body: Chenin and goat's cheese is a Loire classic. Try a dry Vouvray or Saumur with crottin de Chavignol or Sainte-Maure.

steps.prompt: Sweet Loire Chenin can age for 50 years or more.
steps.explanation: Yes. Its high acidity and sugar preserve it.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dry Chenin suits pork and goat's cheese; off-dry suits spice
Serve dry at 10 to 12 degrees, sweet at 8 to 10
